QPP employee contribution rate (base + first additional)

Employee QPP contribution rate, base plus first additional contribution; the employer pays the same amount. 2026: 6.30% (5.30% base + 1%) after the one-year cut of the base rate announced in Finance Québec bulletin 2025-8 and applied by Revenu Québec (amendment of s. 44.1 of the Act respecting the Québec Pension Plan). The bulletin states that the s. 44.1 rule applies again for 2027. Act respecting the Québec Pension Plan, s. 44.1, 50 and 63. Sources: https://www.revenuquebec.ca/documents/en/formulaires/tp/TP-1015.F-V(2026-01).pdf ; https://www.revenuquebec.ca/documents/en/formulaires/tp/TP-1015.F-V(2025-01).pdf ; https://cdn-contenu.quebec.ca/cdn-contenu/adm/min/finances/publications-adm/Bulletins/FR/BULFR_2025-8.pdf ; https://www.legisquebec.gouv.qc.ca/en/document/cs/R-9

Base part of the employee QPP rate. The remainder (rate - base_rate) is the first additional contribution, deductible in the Quebec (CSA of TP-1015.F-V) and federal (F5A of T4127) formulas. Sources: https://www.revenuquebec.ca/documents/en/formulaires/tp/TP-1015.F-V(2026-01).pdf ; https://www.revenuquebec.ca/documents/en/formulaires/tp/TP-1015.F-V(2025-01).pdf ; https://cdn-contenu.quebec.ca/cdn-contenu/adm/min/finances/publications-adm/Bulletins/FR/BULFR_2025-8.pdf ; https://www.legisquebec.gouv.qc.ca/en/document/cs/R-9

Employee rate of the second additional QPP contribution (QPP2) on pensionable earnings between the MPE and the additional MPE; the employer pays the same amount. Remuneration paid up to the end of the month the employee turns this age is not pensionable under the QPP (RL-1.G-V, box G). Act respecting the Québec Pension Plan. Sources: https://www.revenuquebec.ca/documents/en/formulaires/rl/RL-1.G-V(2025-12).pdf ; https://www.revenuquebec.ca/documents/en/formulaires/tp/TP-1015.G-V(2026-01).pdf ; https://www.legisquebec.gouv.qc.ca/en/document/cs/R-9

QPP contributions are withheld until December 31 of the year in which the employee reaches this age and stop on January 1 of the following year (TP-1015.G-V section 4.5.5). Unlike the CPP, the QPP has no stop at age 70. Basic personal amount, used as E1 for an employee who did not file form TP-1015.3-V (TP-1015.F-V, variable E1), and as the annual remuneration at or below which a lump-sum payment bears the flat rate l10n_ca.qc.lump_sum_flat_rate (TP-1015.F-V section 2.1.2, note). Quebec indexation rate of the personal income tax system

Indexation rate of the year, read at January 1 of each year. E1 of a TP-1015.3-V filed for an earlier year is multiplied by 1 + the rate of each following year up to the year of the pay (TP-1015.F-V variable E1: "la valeur de la variable E1 pour 2025 multipliée par 1,0205"); the employee does not file a new form for the annual indexation (TP-1015.G-V part 3.4.1). A year without its own version stops the computation. 2026: "Pour 2026, le taux d'indexation du régime d'imposition des particuliers est de 2,05 %" (TP-1015.F-V and TP-1015.G-V, main changes). Sources: https://www.revenuquebec.ca/documents/en/formulaires/tp/TP-1015.F-V(2026-01).pdf ; https://www.revenuquebec.ca/documents/en/publications/tp/TP-1015.G-V(2026-01).pdf ; https://www.legisquebec.gouv.qc.ca/en/document/cs/I-3
Quebec labour-sponsored fund tax credit rate

Rate of the labour-sponsored fund tax credit in the annual tax: Y = (T x I) - K - K1 - (0,14 x E) - (0,15 x P x Q) - (0,15 x P x Q1), Q and Q1 being the amounts withheld per pay for class A shares of the Fonds de solidarité FTQ and class A or B shares of Fondaction (TP-1015.F-V step 2 and appendix 1). Sources: https://www.revenuquebec.ca/documents/en/formulaires/tp/TP-1015.F-V(2026-01).pdf ; https://www.legisquebec.gouv.qc.ca/en/document/cs/I-3
Quebec flat tax on a lump-sum payment - rate

Quebec deduction for workers - annual maximum

Annual maximum of the deduction for workers; the maximum per pay period is this amount divided by P (TP-1015.F-V step 1). Taxation Act, s. 358.0.1. HSF contribution rate in percent per employer sector, as {sector: [a, b]}: W = a + b x S, S being the total payroll in millions bounded by l10n_ca.qc.hsf.payroll_min and payroll_max, the rate rounded half up to two decimals (TP-1015.F-V part 5). Sectors: general (all employers other than primary/manufacturing and public sector), primary_manufacturing (more than 50% of the payroll in NAICS 11, 21, 31-33), public (flat 4.26%). The temporary 2026-2027 exemption of some agriculture, forestry and fishing employers (bulletin 2025-8) is not modelled. Act respecting the Régie de l'assurance maladie du Québec, s. 34. The RL-1 slips and the RL-1 summary (RLZ-1.S) are due on the last day of this month of the following year, as is the payment of the labour standards and WSDRF contributions (RL-1.G-V section 4.2). A deadline on a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday moves to the next business day (TP-1015.G-V part 11.3). A business that ceases operations files within 30 days after the cessation, and an employer that permanently stops its periodic payments because it has no more employees by the 20th of the month after its last payment (RLZ-1.S, filing deadline). Taxation Act and its regulation. Sources: https://www.revenuquebec.ca/documents/en/formulaires/rl/RL-1.G-V(2025-12).pdf ; https://www.revenuquebec.ca/fr/services-en-ligne/formulaires-et-publications/rlz-1-s-g/guide-du-sommaire-1-sommaire-des-retenues-et-des-cotisations-de-lemployeur/ ; https://www.legisquebec.gouv.qc.ca/en/document/cs/I-3
Revenu Québec remittance due day (monthly, quarterly, annual)

Day of the month following the period on which monthly, quarterly and annual remittances of source deductions and employer contributions are due (TP-1015.G-V table 7). Taxation Act, s. 1015 and its regulation. Sources: https://www.revenuquebec.ca/documents/en/formulaires/tp/TP-1015.G-V(2026-01).pdf ; https://www.legisquebec.gouv.qc.ca/en/document/cs/I-3
Revenu Québec twice-monthly remittance split day

Last day of the first twice-monthly remittance period: remuneration paid before the 16th (TP-1015.G-V table 7). Sources: https://www.revenuquebec.ca/documents/en/formulaires/tp/TP-1015.G-V(2026-01).pdf ; https://www.legisquebec.gouv.qc.ca/en/document/cs/I-3
Revenu Québec twice-monthly first due day

Day of the same month on which the remittance for remuneration paid before the 16th is due (TP-1015.G-V table 7). Sources: https://www.revenuquebec.ca/documents/en/formulaires/tp/TP-1015.G-V(2026-01).pdf ; https://www.legisquebec.gouv.qc.ca/en/document/cs/I-3
Revenu Québec twice-monthly second due day

Day of the following month on which the remittance for remuneration paid from the 16th to the end of the month is due (TP-1015.G-V table 7). Sources: https://www.revenuquebec.ca/documents/en/formulaires/tp/TP-1015.G-V(2026-01).pdf ; https://www.legisquebec.gouv.qc.ca/en/document/cs/I-3
Revenu Québec weekly remittance period ends

Last days of the first three weekly remittance periods of a month; the fourth ends on the last day of the month (TP-1015.G-V table 7). Sources: https://www.revenuquebec.ca/documents/en/formulaires/tp/TP-1015.G-V(2026-01).pdf ; https://www.legisquebec.gouv.qc.ca/en/document/cs/I-3
Revenu Québec weekly remittance delay (business days)

A weekly remittance is due on this business day after the last day of the period (TP-1015.G-V table 7). Sources: https://www.revenuquebec.ca/documents/en/formulaires/tp/TP-1015.G-V(2026-01).pdf ; https://www.legisquebec.gouv.qc.ca/en/document/cs/I-3
